group_name: Well Played Blood on the Clocktower Group
summary: This is a $10 ticketed 'Social Deduction Showdown' session of Blood on the Clocktower run biweekly by Well Played Board Game Café in Asheville, capped at 15 players and 'hosted and guided by an experienced storyteller.' Every listing across both units reuses identical generic marketing copy ('Join us for another session of lies, secrets, and murder—can you survive the night?') with no membership language, no named regulars, and no mention of a dedicated club, Discord, or Facebook group for this specific offering. It reads as a commercial recurring game-night product run by the café's staff storyteller, with a rotating paying public rather than a self-organizing community.

evidence.note: Listing says 'Hosted and guided by an experienced storyteller. Limited to 15 players—reserve your spot early!' with $10 ticket price, framing it as a paid, staff-run session rather than a member club.
All 19 combined listings across both units (4 sparse + 15 biweekly) reuse near-identical boilerplate description text, with no mention of members, dues, a group name, or returning-player language.

Well Played's own event page confirms the café runs this as a business offering in a private room; while the café has its own general Discord/social presence, the event listing itself names no specific community or club behind this session.

Web search shows other cities (Triangle, The Hugh, Fayetteville) have dedicated Meetup groups purpose-built around Blood on the Clocktower, but no equivalent dedicated Meetup/Facebook group exists for the Asheville/Well Played sessions—only the venue's own recurring ticketed event.
